profile.reading: This is Ciscos data center at 2260 Chelsea Boulevard in Allen, Texas, officially opened April 18, 2011. The facility was built as an active-active mirror to Ciscos existing Richardson, Texas data center about 15 miles away, with the two sites together forming what Cisco calls a Metro Virtual Data Center supporting Cisco IT Elastic Infrastructure Services, the companys internal enterprise and service cloud, making this an internal corporate data center rather than a public colocation facility or hardware testing lab. Cisco has described the site as fed by two separate 10 megawatt utility feeds from different providers, supplemented by about 400 kilowatts of rooftop solar capacity, though a contemporaneous trade press article about the opening separately cited a 5 megawatt capacity figure, a discrepancy this registry attributes to the two figures describing different things, total available utility feed capacity versus actual IT load, rather than a factual conflict, and records both honestly. The facility holds LEED Gold certification, targets a power usage effectiveness of about 1.35, was engineered to withstand winds up to 175 miles per hour given North Texas tornado risk, uses flywheel based uninterruptible power supply technology rather than batteries, and employs air side economizer cooling to reduce mechanical cooling load. No specific total square footage figure was found in sourcing checked this session. Allen sits in Collin County in the Dallas-Fort Worth metropolitan area, a region that has attracted numerous corporate and technology company data centers over the past two decades due to relatively affordable land, a business friendly Texas regulatory and tax environment, and proximity to major fiber and telecommunications infrastructure serving North Texas, factors that also drew other operators tracked elsewhere in this registry to build in the same broader metro area, including Charles Schwab and Citigroup facilities in nearby Denton and Tarrant counties.
profile.research_note: Fresh research via Baxtel, Data Center Knowledges 2011 coverage of the opening, and Ciscos own blog tour of the facility. The 10 MW versus 5 MW capacity figures found across sources were not reconciled to a single number and are both recorded with an honest explanation of the likely discrepancy (utility feed capacity versus IT load) rather than picking one arbitrarily.

reading.body:
Cisco Allen is a data center campus in Allen, Texas, built in 2010, located at 2260 Chelsea Blvd. The facility's published power capacity and floor area are not available. The operator's specifications do not disclose whether this campus serves AI workloads or any other specific tenant category.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which 18 publish power specifications totaling 468 megawatts. Cisco Allen does not appear in the published capacity rankings for the state, placing it outside the top 18 facilities by disclosed power. The state context provided does not include this campus's megawatt figure.

This campus cannot be assessed for relevance to AI scaling without published specifications on power capacity, IT load density, or cooling infrastructure. Cisco maintains a large networking equipment business separate from its data center operations. Whether this facility operates as a merchant colocation site, hosts company infrastructure, or serves other purposes is not disclosed.
